title: Session-windowed prompt union and compacted KV shard overlays
creator: Michael Chen
description: Background: Our continuous-batching runtime keeps per-request KV entries in GPU memory to accelerate autoregressive decoding. Workloads with many small, similar prompts (slot-filling templates, chat system prompts with different user variables) create near-duplicate KV material that consumes GPU memory and increases eviction churn. This ticket proposes a runtime-first approach that (1) performs session-windowed unionization of prompt segments to merge closely related KV material across concurrent requests, and (2) maintains compact overlay shards with per-shard bloom fingerprints and a lightweight similarity index to deduplicate on-device without expensive host roundtrips. The goal is to reduce resident KV bytes, improve batch packing density, and lower token latency variance during heavy multi-tenant workloads.
goals: Reduce average GPU-resident KV size per concurrent request by >= 30% on template-heavy workloads
Lower eviction-induced cache misses during 95th percentile load spikes
Enable cheap on-GPU similarity checks (sub-microsecond per candidate) and only escalate to embedding checks for borderline cases
Expose a safe feature-flag rollout that allows operator-controlled similarity thresholds and compaction aggressiveness
non_goals: Replace persistent disk-backed cache mechanisms (this work complements, but does not supersede snapshotting)
Provide semantic deduplication across unrelated user sessions or cross-tenant fusion (tenant isolation preserved)
proposal: Design overview: At each batching boundary we open a short (configurable) session window (default: 500ms) keyed by target model, route, and tenant. Within the window we compute cheap signatures for request prompt segments using a rolling simhash + short token ngram fingerprint. Requests that exceed a similarity threshold enter a 'union candidate' set. For each candidate set we build a transient overlay shard on-GPU: a compact index of segment fingerprints, a per-entry refcount and access timestamp, and a small bloom filter to quickly rule out misses. When a new request arrives we attempt to map its segments into the overlay; if a strong match is found we reuse the backing KV slice (increment refcount) instead of materializing a duplicate slice. For ambiguous matches we launch a limited-cost cosine check against stored segment embeddings (host-side if necessary) but with early-abort heuristics. Compaction: periodic background jobs coalesce overlay shards that exceed a fragmentation threshold and rewrite contiguous KV slabs to remove padding and free GPU pages. Eviction policy: augment existing LRU with an access-heat decay that prefers retaining unionized shared slices and targets ephemeral single-use duplicates for reclamation.
implementation_details: On-GPU data structures: 64-bit fingerprint table, 16-byte per-entry metadata (refcount, last-access, flags), preallocated slab chains for KV slices
Batching hooks: extend batching coordinator to expose session window grouping and candidate set enumeration
Similarity pipeline: simhash for initial grouping (Hamming threshold), MinHash for quick Jaccard approx on token sets, embedding cosine fallback with early cutoffs
Consistency: refcount increments are atomic on GPU. Shard compaction uses copy-on-write with a short grace period to avoid invalidating in-flight decoders
Config knobs: session_window_ms, simhash_hamming_thresh, bloom_fp_rate, compaction_fragmentation_pct, embed_check_limit_per_window
Telemetry: per-shard reuse rate, bytes-saved, compaction time, embedding-fallback-count, refcount distribution
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for fingerprint collisions and early-abort logic
Deterministic integration tests with mocked batching coordinator to validate refcount lifecycle
Performance microbench: synthetic template-heavy workload (10k requests/min, 75% template overlap) measuring resident KV bytes and tail latency
Chaos tests: simulate worker preemption and network jitter during compaction to verify safe rollbacks
A/B canary in staging with 10% traffic then 50% traffic comparing token cost and 95th latency
acceptance_criteria: Staging canary reduces mean resident KV bytes per worker by >= 30% on template workload
No increase >2% in token error rate (change in generated outputs) across canary compared to baseline
No regression in 99th percentile latency beyond 10% after compaction stabilization
Operational metrics (compaction failures, refcount anomalies) are zero or explainable and resolved before promote
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gated implementation merged behind runtime-1.20 feature flags
Dev-stage canary with synthetic templates (internal tools) - 03/18 to 03/21
Staging canary on customer-like traffic (10%) - 03/22 to 03/26
Gradual ramp to 50% with monitoring - 03/27 to 03/30
Full rollout conditional on metrics - target 04/05
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Fingerprint collisions cause false reuse and degrade output. Mitigation: conservative simhash thresholds, embedding fallback verification for ambiguous merges
Risk: Compaction stalls or copies large slabs causing latency spikes. Mitigation: run compaction in low-priority background queue with IO/copy rate limiters and observability to abort long jobs
Risk: Cross-tenant safety bug. Mitigation: shard keys include tenant identifier; integration test includes multi-tenant scenarios
Risk: Increased host-GPU syncs due to embedding checks. Mitigation: limit embed_check_per_window and batch embedding verifications to amortize cost

notes: This approach favors runtime-local, low-cost heuristics and opportunistic compaction to avoid host-side bottlenecks. It is intentionally conservative about cross-tenant fusion to preserve compliance boundaries. Implementation will iterate on thresholds driven by staging telemetry.
